correctness.rationale: The five affine images give the support rows starting at 1,1,1,2,4,5,…, with expansion uniformly greater than 1 for fixed λ. Closed walks to state 1 are finite at each length since sufficiently high states can descend at most one level per step. With r=(3−√5)/2 and β=2+√5, the tail sum gives Aw=βw for w₁=w₂=w₃=1, wᵢ=2r^(i−3) otherwise: the identity in the tail is βr(1−r)=1, and states 1–3 and 4 supply the two stated finite boundary equations. The Doob transform is irreducible and aperiodic with a strictly negative drift −1+r/(1−r) outside a finite set, proving positive recurrence and return growth β. For either this chain or the acip chain with tail parameter p=r or p=λ<1/2, V(i)=a^i with 1<a<(1−p)/p has a strict multiplicative Foster contraction outside the finite head, since E[V(J)|i]/V(i)=(1−p)/(a(1−pa))<1. Hence the stationary state index has finite mean (indeed a finite exponential moment) and finite one-state entropy. This justifies the entropy-rate/generator step and makes log w integrable for the Doob chain. In stationarity −log Qᵢⱼ=logβ+log wᵢ−log wⱼ averages to logβ, confirming maximal entropy. Affinity preserves conditional cell uniformity given every finite past itinerary for the acip, so the metric entropy is the Shannon entropy of the geometric row. Its derivative and the limits at 0 and 1/2 give the claimed strict gap and infimum. The frozen symbolic/truncation checker was inspected, not run; finite truncations are not a proof of the growth rate.

evidence: For fixed length n only finitely many first-return paths to B={1,2,3} are possible from state 1. Divide every Pᵢⱼ by 1−λ and take λ↑1; each allowed edge tends to weight 1. Since all three initial rows coincide, the first-return series starting at 1 is thus R(z)=lim Fλ(z/(1−λ)) coefficientwise. Using the explicit formula gives R(z)=3z+2z(1−s)/(1+s), s=√(1−4z).

Renewal of visits to B gives 1/(1−R(z)) and the counts returning to 1 are one step later than visits to B (only the three base states have an edge to 1). The first positive solution of R(z)=1 is ρ=√5−2<1/4, with finite R′(ρ), giving h_G=−logρ and finite-mean normalized first returns, the positive-recurrent case. Ji–Ma’s geometric transition rows and acip give the metric entropy by summing a geometric Shannon entropy; the gap is then immediate.

value.rationale: The entropy gap is a meaningful comparison on a natural auxiliary system, and the Doob transform is a useful alternative proof. But the exact growth, positive recurrence, and final entropy gap follow directly from the indexed exact first-return law and Ji–Ma’s geometric kernel. Under the criterion for a narrow exact invariant, there is no independently needed unknown invariant left in this record; no stronger genuinely distinct result about the original bimodal map is claimed.
